text:
Find host resource and service problems before choosing a fix. Read system, network, storage and certificate facts without changing the host. Start with load or disks; available sections depend on the Linux account running this agent.
all: Review every section available to the agent's Linux account. Disk health and hardware sensor sections require root.
system: Identify the host and its running kernel.
network: Inspect network interfaces and routes.
memory: Check memory and swap usage.
disks: Inspect disks and check free filesystem space.
load: Check system load and process counts.
tls: Check the public TLS certificate's fingerprint, names and expiry, including days left. Compare its fingerprint with the token helper's pin.
uptime: Check how long the host has run and its load averages.
os: Identify the operating system distribution.
cpu: Inspect processor architecture and topology.
inodes: Check filesystem inode usage, which can prevent new files even when bytes remain free.
pressure: Check how much CPU, memory and input/output contention delays work.
units: Find failed services and other systemd units.
time: Check the clock and whether it is synchronized.
dns: Inspect the host's name-resolution configuration.
ports: Find listening TCP sockets.
users: See which users are logged in.
virt: Identify the virtualization type. A bare-metal host reports none.
health: Inspect disk health. This section requires the agent to run as root.
sensors: Read hardware temperatures and other sensor values. This section requires the agent to run as root.

Examples
agent-bus call '#server-info@parf.us' 'system'
agent-bus call '#server-info@parf.us' 'memory'
agent-bus call '#server-info@parf.us' 'disks'
